output.title: Dollar threshold for escalating a specialty pharmacy case to the pharmacy director
output.draft_text:
When a specialty pharmacy case exceeds the cost threshold, it must be escalated to the pharmacy director for review.

Threshold: A specialty case is routed to the pharmacy director when [the cost measure, e.g., per-claim cost, monthly cost, or annualized cost of therapy] is [greater than / greater than or equal to] [dollar amount].

What counts toward the threshold: [Describe which costs are included, e.g., ingredient cost only, total allowed amount, or plan-paid amount, and whether member cost share is included or excluded].

How to escalate:
1. Confirm the case meets the threshold using [system or report used to verify cost].
2. Document [required information, e.g., member ID, drug name, NDC, prescriber, cost calculation, clinical notes].
3. Send the case to the pharmacy director through [escalation channel, e.g., queue name, form, or email address].
4. Tell the member or provider [approved member-facing language about the review], including the expected decision time of [number of business days].

Exceptions: [List any drugs, drug classes, plan types, or urgent/expedited situations that follow a different threshold or route].

If the pharmacy director is unavailable: [backup approver or alternate route].

If you are unsure whether a case meets the threshold, [whom to contact, e.g., supervisor or clinical pharmacist].

author_checklist: Confirm the exact dollar threshold from the governing pharmacy policy or delegation-of-authority document and cite the source.
Confirm which cost measure the threshold applies to (per claim, monthly, annualized) and what costs are included.
Confirm whether the threshold is inclusive (at or above) or exclusive (above).
Confirm whether the threshold differs by plan type, line of business, drug class, or client contract.
Confirm the escalation channel, required documentation, and the expected turnaround time.
Confirm the backup approver when the pharmacy director is unavailable.
Confirm the handling of urgent or expedited cases and any regulatory decision timeframes that apply.
Confirm the approved language advocates may use with members and providers.
Have the pharmacy director or a pharmacy policy owner review and approve the final content.
Set an effective date and a review date, because thresholds may change.
